intro: Business and market vocabulary, and how to imagine what would have happened if things had been different.
p.empresa.consejo: It comes from «emprender». There are large, medium and small companies («pymes»).
p.socio.consejo: Feminine: «socia». A partner puts money or work into the company. You can also be a club member.
p.sede.consejo: The secondary offices are «sucursales». You also hear «la sede de un congreso».
p.sucursal.consejo: A bank or a shop has its headquarters in one place and branches in others.
p.demanda.consejo: It goes with «oferta»: «la oferta y la demanda». You say «hay mucha demanda» or «poca demanda».
p.oferta.consejo: Two meanings: «la oferta y la demanda» and «estar de oferta», which is to be on sale.
p.competencia.consejo: In business they are the rivals. A sports race is «una competición». It also means «skill».
p.pedido.consejo: You say «hacer un pedido» and «recibir un pedido». It comes from «pedir».
p.proveedor.consejo: It comes from «proveer»: to supply what is needed. A supplier delivers goods to a shop.
p.lanzamiento.consejo: It comes from «lanzar». You say «el lanzamiento de un producto» or «de un libro».
p.marca.consejo: It is also a mark on something: «una marca en la pared». You say «una marca conocida».
p.rentable.consejo: It works for masculine and feminine: «un negocio rentable», «una tienda rentable».
p.beneficio.consejo: It also means «advantage»: «un beneficio para todos». Its financial opposite is «pérdida».
p.quebrar.consejo: The e becomes ie: «quiebro», «quiebras», «quiebra». A company that goes bankrupt closes.
b1.texto:
**The company.** A **empresa** has a **sede** and sometimes **sucursales**. It is formed by one or more **socios**. Its **marca** is the name the public knows it by.

**The market.** **Oferta** is what is offered; **demanda**, what people want to buy. **La competencia** are the rival companies. A business is **rentable** if it makes **beneficios**; if not, it loses money and may **quebrar**.

**Buying and selling.** A shop places a **pedido** with its **proveedor**, who sends the goods. A new product needs a **lanzamiento**, usually with an advertising campaign.

**If I had… I would have…** To talk about what did not happen we use **si + hubiera + participle** and **habría + participle**: **Si hubiéramos lanzado la marca antes, habríamos tenido menos competencia.**
b2.f0.texto: The launch of the new brand is on Friday.
b2.f1.texto: The market research says there is a lot of demand.
b2.f2.texto: The competition also sells cheaper trainers.
b2.f3.texto: If we had launched the brand earlier, we would have had less competition.
b2.f4.texto: The supplier has already sent the goods to the headquarters.
b2.f5.texto: Every branch has placed a big order.
b2.f6.texto: If the campaign works, the business will be profitable this year.
b2.f7.texto: The partners do not want the company to go bankrupt.
b4.titulo: What did not happen: if I had… I would have…
b4.texto:
**Si + hubiera/hubiese + participle, habría + participle** talks about something that did not happen and its imagined result: **Si hubiéramos lanzado la marca antes, habríamos tenido menos competencia.** (We did not launch earlier and had more competition.)

- **Hubiera** and **hubiese** are equivalent: **si hubiese hecho** or **si hubiera hecho**.
- After **si** the conditional is never used: you do not say «si habríamos esperado».
- For something unreal in the present, **si + imperfect subjunctive, conditional**: **Si tuviéramos más socios, abriríamos otra sucursal.**
b4.e0.texto: If they had listened to the research, they would never have launched the product.
b4.e1.texto: If we had more partners, we would open a branch in Bilbao.
b4.e2.texto: If the offer had been better, demand would have risen.
b5.titulo: From a garage to forty countries
b5.f0.texto: In a garage in Alicante it smelled of hot rubber and glue.
b5.f1.texto: Two partners cut plastic bottles under a bare bulb.
b5.f2.texto: Their tired hands sewed the soles with thick thread and patience.
b5.f3.texto: According to the market research, nobody would buy those trainers.
b5.f4.texto: Every night they counted the losses with a heavy heart.
b5.f5.texto: One rainy morning, an actress posed with a pair of green trainers in front of the cameras.
b5.f6.texto: The photograph ran across the screens of the world like a spark on dry grass.
b5.f7.texto: Within a week the garage telephone rang without rest.
b5.f8.texto: The orders arrived in heaps like autumn leaves.
b5.f9.texto: Today the brand sells in forty countries from a small, bright headquarters.
b6.o0: Si hubiéramos esperado, habríamos perdido clientes
b6.o0.refuerzo: Yes: si + hubiéramos + participle, habríamos + participle.
b6.o1: Si habríamos esperado, habríamos perdido clientes
b6.o1.refuerzo: After «si» the conditional is not used.
b6.o2.refuerzo: The second part needs the conditional perfect.
b7.frase: Si hubieran hecho caso, nunca ____ lanzado el producto.
b7.o0.refuerzo: That is the present perfect; here you need the conditional.
b7.o2.refuerzo: That is the past perfect indicative; it does not fit with «si hubieran».
b7.pregunta: Which form completes the conditional perfect?
b8.frase: Hicimos un pedido al proveedor la semana pasada
b8.traduccion: We placed an order with the supplier last week
b9.o1.refuerzo: It can mean skill, but a skill does not sell anything.
b9.o2.refuerzo: Yes: in the market, «la competencia» are the rival companies.
b9.pregunta: What is «la competencia» in «la competencia vende más barato»?
b11.o0.refuerzo: Yes: de + article + que, agreeing with «pedidos» (masculine plural).
b11.o1.refuerzo: Before a verb you need «de los que».
b11.o2.refuerzo: «Lo» does not agree with «pedidos»: you need «los».
b12.o0.refuerzo: «Quebrar» is to run out of money and close.
b12.o1.refuerzo: Yes: «rentable» is what makes more money than it costs.
b12.o2.refuerzo: «Estar de oferta» is to have a reduced price.
b12.pregunta: What is a business that makes money like?
p.vende.consejo: From «vender», to sell; the «v» sounds like «b».
p.zapatillas.consejo: Plural of «zapatilla»; the «z» sounds like «th» in Spain.
p.hubiéramos.consejo: Used after «si» for something that did not happen: «si hubiéramos esperado».
p.lanzado.consejo: Past participle of «lanzar», to launch something.
p.enviado.consejo: Past participle of «enviar», to send; the «v» sounds like «b».
p.mercancía.consejo: Goods for sale; in Spain the «cí» sounds like «thi».
p.negocio.consejo: «Negocio» is a business; «negociar» means to negotiate.
p.socios.consejo: Plural of «socio», a partner in a business.
p.quiebre.consejo: Subjunctive of «quebrar», to go bankrupt, after «que».
p.hubieran.consejo: Like «hubiéramos», used after «si» for something that did not happen.
p.caso.consejo: In «hacer caso», it means to pay attention to advice.
p.habrían.consejo: Conditional of «haber» for «ellos»: what would have happened.
p.tuviéramos.consejo: Subjunctive of «tener» in «si» sentences: if we had.
p.abriríamos.consejo: Conditional of «abrir» for «nosotros»: what we would do.
p.pegamento.consejo: From «pegar», to stick; «pegamento» is what makes things stick.
p.cortaban.consejo: Imperfect of «cortar» for «ellos»: an action going on in the past.
p.cosían.consejo: Imperfect of «coser», to sew; the accent on «í» gives two syllables.
p.suelas.consejo: Plural of «suela», the bottom part of a shoe.
p.aquellas.consejo: «Aquellas» points to far away things, feminine plural.
p.contaban.consejo: Imperfect of «contar» for «ellos»: something repeated in the past.
p.encogido.consejo: Past participle of «encoger», to shrink; «corazón encogido» means a heavy heart.
p.posó.consejo: Past tense of «posar», to pose for a photo; the «ó» takes the stress.
p.par.consejo: «Un par de» means a pair of something.
p.chispa.consejo: A «chispa» is a tiny spark that jumps from fire or metal.
p.sonaba.consejo: Imperfect of «sonar», to ring: it went on in the past.
p.pedidos.consejo: Plural of «pedido», an order for goods.
p.llegaban.consejo: Imperfect of «llegar» for «ellos»: going on for a while.
p.montones.consejo: Plural of «montón», a big pile of things.
p.hicimos.consejo: Past tense of «hacer» for «nosotros»; the «c» sounds like «th».
p.empresas.consejo: Plural of «empresa», a company or firm.
p.rivales.consejo: «Rival» means competing: the other company after the same customers.
p.recibieron.consejo: Third person plural in the past of «recibir»; the «c» sounds like «th».
p.podían.consejo: Imperfect of «poder» for «ellos»: what they were able to do.
p.atender.consejo: Infinitive of «atender», to serve or look after customers.
